blacklistabilityReview.evidence: Explicit Direct retained: incident reporting and the local obituary record that Resolv burned unbacked USR supply via a blacklist freeze after the March 2026 exploit.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: USR is natively issued on Ethereum; LayerZero V2 connects the Ethereum USR lockbox to six burn/mint SimpleOFT representations. Remote token-level minting is externally authenticated and supply-conserving only while adapter lock/remote burn accounting, peer authentication, endpoint/DVN checks, and upgrade controls hold; the route is assessed here rather than as native Mint Authority.

controls.label: Ethereum USR adapter owner Safe

routeChecks.lockboxOrEscrow: The Ethereum SimpleOFTAdapter holds canonical USR and locks/unlocks it for LayerZero transfers; it does not create an independent native liability.
routeChecks.trustedPeerOrRemote: Adapter peers bind the route to Base, BSC, Berachain, HyperEVM, Arbitrum, and Soneium representations; remote peer mesh is also configured.
routeChecks.rateLimits: No application-level rate-limit contract was identified; endpoint-level rate limiting and exact ULN/DVN/Executor getConfig remain unverified.
routeChecks.pausersAdminsUpgraders: The Safe owns adapter configuration including peers and delegate-related bridge settings; the separate ProxyAdmin Timelock controls adapter upgrades.

sources.label: Ethereum USR token and Safe review

controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25770505, the 4-of-6 Safe owns the LayerZero adapter that locks and unlocks canonical USR and controls its bridge peer configuration. This bridge capability is separate from the native SERVICE_ROLE mint path; supply conservation depends on adapter lock/remote burn accounting and authenticated LayerZero peers.

controls.label: base USR SimpleOFT owner Safe

routeChecks.trustedPeerOrRemote: The owner controls setPeer and related LayerZero route configuration; the Ethereum EID 30101 peer is the canonical adapter and the representation also participates in the verified satellite mesh.
routeChecks.rateLimits: No application-level rate-limit contract was identified; endpoint-level rate limiting and exact ULN/DVN/Executor getConfig remain unverified.
routeChecks.pausersAdminsUpgraders: The owner controls peer/delegate, enforced-options, message-inspector, and pre-crime settings; no separate pause controller was identified. The legacy guard selector reverted, so guard status remains unknown.

controls.evidence: At base block 50064097, this 4-of-6 Safe owns the destination SimpleOFT configuration. Its empty module read and the unresolved legacy guard read are retained; it can change peer/authentication settings that determine whether remote receive minting remains constrained to the LayerZero route.

controls.label: Ethereum USR adapter ProxyAdmin Timelock

routeChecks.pausersAdminsUpgraders: The Timelock owns the adapter ProxyAdmin and can replace canonical-side bridge logic with zero enforced delay; this is bridge upgrade authority, not the native SERVICE_ROLE mint gate.
routeChecks.unsupportedReason: Exact LayerZero endpoint ULN/DVN/Executor getConfig values and rate limits remain unverified.

controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25770505, ProxyAdmin owner 0x290d9544669c9c7a64f6899a0a3b28d563f6ebee controls the adapter upgrade path and reports getMinDelay() = 0. The adverse upgrade domain is preserved under Bridge Risk; the native token's own upgrade and SERVICE_ROLE controls remain in Mint Authority.
